The life span for the lower grade of the Sphere of Infinite Space (ākāśānantyāyatana) is seventeen thousand five hundred great kalpas; the life span for the middle grade of the Sphere of Infinite Space is eighteen thousand five hundred great kalpas; and the life span for the upper grade of the Sphere of Infinite Space is twenty thousand great kalpas.

The life span of the gods in the lower grade of the Sphere of Infinite Consciousness is thirty thousand great kalpas; the life span of those in the middle grade of the Sphere of Infinite Consciousness is thirty-five thousand great kalpas; and the life span of those in the upper grade of the Sphere of Infinite Consciousness is forty thousand great kalpas.

The life span of the gods in the lower grade of the Sphere of Nothingness (ākiṃcanyāyatana) is fifty thousand great kalpas; the life span of the gods in the middle grade of the Sphere of Nothingness is fifty-five thousand great kalpas; and the life span of the gods in the upper grade of the Sphere of Nothingness is sixty thousand great kalpas.

The life span of those in the lower grade of the Heaven of Neither Perception nor Non-perception is seventy thousand great kalpas; the life span of those in the middle grade of the Heaven of Neither Perception nor Non-perception is seventy-five thousand great kalpas; and the life span of those in the upper grade of the Heaven of Neither Perception nor Non-perception is eighty thousand great kalpas.
This meaning was spoken by the Buddha, the World-Honored One.
Thus have I heard.
*Lishi Apitan Lun*, Fascicle Seven.
The *Lishi Apitan Lun* (Treatise on the Abhidharma of the Establishment of the World), translated by the Tripiṭaka Master Paramārtha of Western India during the Chen Dynasty, Volume Eight.

Chapter Twenty-Three: The Section on Hells. Part One: The Hell of Rebirth. Chapter Twenty-Three: The Section on Hells 1. The Hell of Rebirth (Saṃjīva) [The text continues with the description of the Saṃjīva hell.]
"In the past, present, and future worlds, the births, deaths, declines, arisings, and cycles of sentient beings are witnessed by the Buddha, the World-Honored One.
No karmic actions are in vain; there are fruits and retributions that are never lost."
Maturing beings according to the time and place, the noble wise one awakens by himself.
Gautama understands this teaching; the World-Honored One has fully realized and seen the eight great hells, becoming the eye of all dharmas.
Saṃjīva and Kālasūtra, The two places of Screaming (Raurava) and Great Screaming (Mahāraurava),
The two places of Heating (Tapana) and Great Heating (Pratāpana), And the great Avīci—
These eight hells, the Buddha taught, are difficult to cross.
Evil beings constantly fill it; each section has sixteen partitions.
At its four corners and four gates, every division is perfectly equal.
It rises a hundred yojanas high, and extends a hundred yojanas in each of the four directions.
Encircled by iron walls, with an iron lid covering them above;
the ground below is entirely iron, filled everywhere with blazing flames.
It burns the wicked and is terrifying, constantly aflame and difficult to approach.
Those who see it will surely have their hair stand on end; its extreme suffering is unbearable to behold.
Now I shall explain it for you in the proper sequence according to the Dharma;
listen with reverence and a single mind to my words as I speak them.
“There is a hell named Saṃjīva (Reviving), which is entirely made of iron; it burns day and night, constantly emitting flames, measuring many yojanas in length and likewise in breadth.”
In this place, the wardens seize the sinners, holding them with their feet up and heads down according to the Black Rope Division, and hack them with adzes.

Once they have been hacked until nothing remains but bones held together by tendons, they faint and die for a brief moment; then, amidst this most extreme and heavy suffering, the wardens cast them aside.
At that time, a cold wind blows upon them and they are restored to life; by means of this wind, their skin and flesh return to their normal state.
Then, the hands and claws of these offenders naturally grow back, hard and sharp like swords. They give rise to feelings of mutual resentment toward their own kind and think to themselves:
"This person previously committed such evil against me; therefore, I shall quickly harm him first."
The arising of their malicious intent is likewise so;
they hack at one another as if mowing down a thicket of hemp.

These hell-beings undergo such mutual injury, experiencing suffering of the highest degree that is difficult to endure—extremely firm, extremely intense, and most agonizingly bitter—and they cannot seek death until the retribution for their evil karma has been fully exhausted.
By what karma and conduct is this retribution produced, causing sentient beings to be born there?
Formerly, among humans, many women shared a single husband and were mutually resentful and jealous;
or, many men contended for a single woman, giving rise to a mind of enmity.

Some commit adultery with the wives of others; some dispute over fields, gardens, carriages, and the like; some kings of two nations contend over neighboring territories; or some plunder the wealth of others and are punished by their owners, thereby forming mutual enmities like men clashing in battle and slaughtering one another.
Having already formed an enmity that has not yet been reconciled, one dies harboring this resentment; through the retribution of this karma, one is reborn there.
Furthermore, due to various kinds of evil and unwholesome karmic retributions, one is born there; furthermore, there is a predominant karma that induces birth there.
Having been born therein, they experience the various karmic retributions of their evil deeds.
By what karmic cause do these sinners further mutilate and hack one another?

Because in their former lives as humans, they wielded axes, hatchets, swords, and other weapons to slaughter and mangle living beings, they therefore undergo this retribution of mutual hacking within that realm.
Furthermore, by what karma are they blown by cold winds and yet revived?

Formerly, while among humans, they raised livestock for food—such as cattle, deer, pigs, sheep, chickens, and ducks—and once these animals had grown fat, they were slaughtered for their abundant flesh. Due to the retribution of this karma, they encounter those cold winds and are granted a temporary return to life.
What kind of karmic retribution results in the birth of talons as sharp as swords?
In a former life among humans, one provided people with weapons such as knives and staves and gave them this instruction:
"You should come to such-and-such a province, prefecture, or county, and go there to commit killings, whether of humans or animals."
“Due to the retribution of this karma, sword-claws arise.
Why is this hell named ‘Rebirth’ (Saṃjīva)?
It is because the sinners therein form this thought:”
"I have now been reborn; my flesh and body are as they were before.
For this reason, it is called "Rebirth" (Saṃjīva).
Furthermore, this hell was originally named Rebirth.
At that time, the World-Honored One, wishing to clarify this meaning once more,
spoke in verse: "Born again within the hells, With head downward and feet upward,
They are seized with axes and other tools, And hacked by the executioners following the cord."
At that time, after being hacked apart, only a heap of bones remains;
yet the flesh, blood, skin, tendons, and so forth, restore themselves to their original state.
Sharp sword-like claws at the tips of the fingers arise spontaneously through the power of karma.
Following their former hearts of resentment and anger, they hack and strike one another.
After having endured this mutual slaughter, a cold wind blows once more, causing all their limbs and members to regenerate;
this is brought about by the karma of the "contentious wind."
The Tathāgata, teacher of gods and humans, having seen this as it truly is,
therefore spoke of the place where those who commit evil are reborn.
The Chapter on Rebirth in Hell is concluded.

2. Second, the Black Rope Hell and the Great Street Hell. Regarding the second, the Black Rope Hell: "Furthermore, there is a hell named Black Rope; everything therein is made of iron. Day and night it burns, with fires that are constantly ablaze and radiant. It is many yojanas in length, and its breadth is likewise."

Therein, the wardens seize the offenders and force them to lie upon the ground, like felling a living tree; they then mark out black lines and hack them with adzes, fashioning them into shapes of eight corners, six corners, or four edges.
There are certain sinners whose bodies, from the heels of their feet up to their necks, are hewn and chopped with axes and hatchets like sections of sugarcane;
there are others whose bodies, from the neck down to the feet, are finely sliced with axes and hatchets, likewise like sections of sugarcane.

These hell-beings undergo this slaughter and mutilation; the suffering of the highest degree is difficult to endure, being most solid, most intense, and most agonizing. Thus they remain until their evil karma has been fully exhausted, at which point they cannot even seek death.
By what kind of karma is this retribution produced, causing sentient beings to be born there? In former times, while among humans, they performed such deeds:

according to the laws and regulations of the world, and according to the measurements of the world, they themselves committed or incited others to inflict such severe punishments—such as having their hands severed in such great quantities, or having their feet severed in such measures; likewise for the cutting off of noses and ears;

and likewise for having such great quantities of flesh cut from their backs, or from both thighs, whether five *liang* or ten *liang*. Due to the retribution of this karma, these sentient beings take birth therein.
Furthermore, various kinds of evil and unwholesome karmic retributions arise within that birth; moreover, there are superior karmas that induce rebirth therein.
Having been born there, one experiences various kinds of evil and unwholesome karmic retributions.
"Sometimes within that place, the hell-wardens revile those who have received their punishment out of fear, saying:
'Evil men! Arise, arise! Do not move!
At that time, the hearts of the immeasurable sinners are struck with great terror, and they all stand upright and motionless at once, like a forest of banners."

At that time, iron garments and iron *kāṣāyas* were constantly burning with fire, emitting great flames and radiance; countless tens of millions of red iron *kāṣāyas* and red iron garments descended from the sky.
At that time, the various sinners cried out:
"This garment! This garment!"

Once these garments have arrived, each person is individually wrapped in them; their skin, flesh, sinews, and bones are all scorched and rotted away. When they have been completely scorched and rotted, the iron garments depart of their own accord.

These hell-beings undergo this burning and roasting; it is a suffering of the highest degree, difficult to endure, extremely firm and intense, and most agonizingly bitter. Thus, until the retribution for their evil karma is fully exhausted, they cannot seek death even if they long for it.
By what karma did they receive this retribution, causing sentient beings to be born there?
In their past lives among humans, they seized whips and staves to beat and lash living beings—whether with leather whips, rattan vines, or even fish-tail whips—to torment them.

Furthermore, there are those who have left the household life but broken their precepts, yet still enjoy the use of the kingdom's lands, clothing, and waist-bands; by the karmic retribution of this, they are born therein.
Moreover, various kinds of evil and unwholesome fruits of retribution arise within that place.
Furthermore, there are those who, through superior karma, are reborn in that intermediate state.
Having been reborn in that intermediate state, they experience various retributions for their unwholesome karma.
There are certain sinners whose jailers flay their skin, starting from the heels up to the neck, but do not allow it to be completely removed.
Furthermore, the hell-wardens flay the skin from the offenders' necks down to their heels, yet do not completely separate it from the body.

Again, there are offenders whose skin is flayed from the neck to the waist, or from the waist to the heels, causing the skin worn upon their bodies to hang down, trail, and drag all the way to the ground; as they tread upon it themselves, the suffering is unbearable.
For example, just as the garments worn by people of the world are neither even nor uniform in their length and width, so too is the skin upon which these hell-beings are subjected.

These denizens of hell undergo their own flaying and hacking; the suffering is of the highest grade, difficult to endure, extremely firm and intense, and most acutely agonizing. Thus they remain until the retribution for their evil karma is exhausted, at which point they cannot seek death even if they wish for it.
By what karma do beings undergo this retribution and take birth there?

Formerly, while among humans, they committed such deeds as having living beings born to them flayed, so that their skin did not come off but remained upon their bodies like garments, for the sake of amusement and sport;
furthermore, while formerly among humans, they whipped and lashed sentient beings, either acting on their own initiative or at the instruction of others.
Furthermore, there are those who, having left the household life but violated the precepts, enjoy the use of the kingdom’s lands, clothing, bedding, and other requisites;

by the retribution of this karma, they are reborn there. Moreover, various kinds of evil and unwholesome karmic retributions arise within that birth, and furthermore, superior karma brings about rebirth therein.
Having been born therein, they experience the various retributions of their unwholesome karma.
This hell is of extreme darkness, filled with dense smoke whose fumes are acrid and piercing; they split the skin, break the flesh, and penetrate to the bone and the marrow.
This poisonous smoke touches their bodies both internally and externally; the hell-wardens drive and force them into the midst of the smoke before finally setting them down.
These sinners, terrified of and seeking to avoid this smoke, run about in confusion for countless *yojanas*, trampling upon one another’s skin and inflicting mutual suffering.

These hell-beings undergo this smoke-poison, experiencing a suffering of the highest degree that is difficult to endure; it is extremely firm, extremely intense, and most acutely painful, such that as long as the retribution for their evil karma is not yet exhausted, they seek death but cannot obtain it.
By what karmic actions do sentient beings receive this retribution and take birth there?

In former times, while among humans, they constructed high, sealed rooms to kill people with smoke, or built prisons to torment people with smoke; or they were porcupines, pangolins, otters, foxes, wildcats, mice, weasels, or bees and their kin—all of whom were trapped in pits or their own burrows and smoked out. Even mosquitoes and gadflies were driven away by smoke. Through the retribution of such karma, they are born there.
Furthermore, various other evil and unwholesome karmic retributions lead to birth there; moreover, it is through superior karma that one is caused to be born there.
Having been born therein, they experience various retributions for their unwholesome karma.
Why is this hell named Kālasūtra?
Because within it, the sinners are subjected to the realm of black cords, undergoing the agony of being hacked and cut; therefore, it is called Kālasūtra.
Furthermore, its intrinsic nature is originally named "Black Rope.
To restate this meaning, he spoke in verse:
"In the Black Rope hell, the wardens Bind the sinners like trees."
Following the paths of the Kālasūtra realm, they are seized and struck with hatchets and axes.
Furthermore, in the realm of red-hot iron garments, which are constantly burning and glowing day and night, all the sinners are bound and crushed; their flesh and blood flow and dry up.
The skin is flayed from the feet up to the neck, and likewise from the neck down to the waist;
in the Black Rope Hell, the sinners have mostly no skin, leaving only raw red flesh.
In this terrifying darkness, poisonous smoke completely fills the air.
The hell-wardens force them in; once they have entered, they are cast aside.
They run for many *yojanas* through a darkness of smoke where nothing can be seen;
trampling one another’s skin, both self and others suffer together in misery.
Within this, the causes and effects are known by the Buddha as they truly are;
thus he spoke of Kālasūtra, the dwelling place of evil persons.
The Chapter on the Hell of Kālasūtra is concluded.
The Great Street Hell: "Situated between the Saṃjīva and Kālasūtra hells, there is a hell named Mahāpatha, which is like the street of a great marketplace."
Among these, the offenders sometimes lie on their backs, sometimes on their stomachs, or are placed within mortars and pounded with iron pestles.
Some offenders have their bodies sliced and hacked from the feet up to the neck, section by section.
There are some offenders whose skin is stripped off and spread upon the ground, and then their own flesh is cut away and piled upon that skin.

Furthermore, there are other offenders whose hands are severed when the sword is brought down, yet their hands grow back as soon as the sword is raised; by this cause and condition, the mass of their accumulated hands becomes as high as a mountain.

When a sword is brought down upon their feet, ears, noses, or heads, they are severed; yet when the sword is raised, they are restored to life, and the mass of heads, noses, and so forth becomes as high as a mountain.
Thus, until the retribution for their evil karma is fully exhausted, they cannot seek death even if they desire it.
By what kind of karma do sentient beings receive this retribution and take birth there?

Formerly, while among humans, they made their living as butchers and slaughterers, killing sheep, pigs, oxen, and deer; or they caught fish and birds, or served as judges in prisons; or they committed robbery and theft themselves, or acted as executioners for criminals.
Through the retribution of such karma, they are born there. Furthermore, various other evil karmas lead to birth there, and additionally, superior karma induces birth in that place.
Having been born therein, they experience various retributions for their unwholesome karma.
These hell-beings have heads like those of elephants and bodies like those of humans;
furthermore, there are other sinners whose heads are like those of horses and whose bodies are like those of humans.
Furthermore, there are other sinners whose heads resemble those of oxen and whose bodies likewise resemble those of humans;
such types as these differ in many ways.
Among them, the hell-wardens seize the sinners and yoke them to iron chariots that burn day and night with constant flames of fire, using red-hot iron for the yokes and red-hot iron for the reins.

The ground along this path is entirely made of iron, extending for many yojanas in length and likewise in breadth; within it, the wardens seize red-hot iron spikes and drive them back and forth, crowding and pressing the beings together.

Undergoing such harm, they experience suffering of the highest degree that is difficult to endure; it is extremely firm, exceedingly intense, and most piercingly agonizing, such that as long as the retribution for their evil karma has not been fully exhausted, they cannot seek death even if they desire it.
By what karma do they receive this retribution, such that sentient beings are born therein?
Formerly, while among humans, they were perhaps elephant trainers, horse trainers, or trainers of oxen and other mounts; by the retribution of such karma, they are born there.
Furthermore, various kinds of evil karmic retributions lead to birth there; it is through the power of predominant karmic retribution that they are caused to be born in that place.
Having been born therein, they experience various kinds of unwholesome retributions.

Among them, there are further sentient beings with the heads of oxen and human bodies; likewise, there are those with the heads of deer and human bodies, and others with the heads of pigs and human bodies—such types as these are of countless varieties.
Numerous hell-wardens gather and surround them, wielding bows, swords, and various weapons to hack and stab the offenders.

Undergoing such torment, they experience the highest grade of suffering, which is difficult to endure, extremely firm and intense, and most agonizingly bitter; thus, as long as the retribution for their evil karma is not exhausted, they cannot seek death even if they wish for it.
By what karma do sentient beings receive such retribution and take birth there?

In former times, while among humans, they wielded blades and staves, hunting and netting living beings; surrounded by many others, they would hack, pierce, kill, or harm them. Through such karmas as these, they take birth there.
Furthermore, various kinds of evil karmic retributions lead to birth there, and there are also superior karmic retributions that induce birth there.
Having been born therein, they experience various retributions for their unwholesome karma.
In that place there is a tree named *Viloma-kaṇṭaka-śālmali*, which is made entirely of iron; it burns day and night, constantly emitting flames of light.
The tree is one yojana high, and its thorns are sixteen inches long.
Therein, the hell-wardens seize the arms of the offenders, pull them up the thorny tree, and then pull them down again.
When pulling it upward, the prongs point downward; when pulling it downward, the prongs point upward.
When pulling it up or down, if the belly touches the tree, the skin and flesh are completely stripped away;
if the back touches the tree, the skin and flesh are likewise stripped away.

The skin and flesh of its belly grow back again, and the skin and flesh of its flanks and back likewise grow back entirely; because of this, it is pulled up and down along with its belly, flanks, and back.

Thus these sinners undergo this torment; the suffering of the highest-of-the-high degree is difficult to endure, being extremely firm, extremely intense, and most agonizing. They do not seek death, nor can they find it, until their evil karma has been fully exhausted.
What karma was performed in the past to receive this retribution, causing sentient beings to be born there?

In the past, among human beings, they committed sexual misconduct with the wives of others, or some women betrayed their husbands; by such karmas as these, they are born there. Furthermore, various kinds of evil karmic retributions lead to birth there, and additionally, superior karmic retributions also lead to birth there.
Having been born therein, they experience various retributions for their unwholesome karma.
Within that hell, there are furthermore many mountains of red-hot iron coals, burning day and night with constant flames.
Therein, the hell-wardens seize the arms of the offenders and pull them up and down; as their bellies are pressed against the mountain, their skin and flesh are completely scorched;
if their backs are pressed against the mountain, their skin and flesh are likewise consumed.
The abdomen returns to its former state, and the skin and flesh of the back and flanks grow back in the same way; because of this, they are pulled up and down along with the belly, flanks, and back.

Thus the sinner undergoes these tortures, suffering the highest grade of pain that is difficult to endure—extremely firm, extremely intense, and most acutely agonizing—until their evil karma has been fully exhausted, at which point they cannot even seek death.
What karma was performed in the past to receive this retribution, such that sentient beings are born there?

In former times, while among humans, they would seize living beings and cast them into fire, or into hot sand, or into hot ashes, or into impure filth; or they would yoke oxen or horses to carriages and travel over hot sand. Through such karmas as these, they are reborn there.
Furthermore, various other evil karmic retributions lead to birth there, and there are also superior karmic retributions that induce birth in that place.
Having been born therein, they undergo various retributions for their unwholesome karma.
Chapter Three: The Hell of Crushing (Saṃghāta). "Furthermore, there is a hell named Saṃghāta; its appearance is like that of the space between two mountains."
Within this place, the hell-wardens brandish various weapons and instruments to terrify the offenders; at that time, the offenders, all filled with fear, enter between the two mountains.

After countless thousands of people had entered the center of the mountain, a great mass of fire blocked the path ahead. At that time, when the sinners saw this fierce fire, they wished to retreat; yet seeing another great mass of fire behind them, they were terrified and writhed about, as the two mountains then closed together.
When the two mountains approach, all the sinners cry out with these words:
"The mountains have come!
The mountains have come!"
The mountains then closed together like oil being pressed from sesame seeds; the mountains pressing down upon the sinners was just like this.

Once the pressing was finished, the mountains opened upward, and when these sinners saw the mountains rising up, they scrambled to enter beneath them, whereupon the mountains immediately fell back down, crushing their bodies once more.
It is like when various wild beasts are pressed and crushed together until their blood flows into rivers, leaving only sinews and bones with no skin or flesh remaining.

Undergoing such slaughter and injury, they experience the most superior grade of suffering, which is difficult to endure; it is extremely firm and intense, the very height of agony, such that as long as the retribution for their evil karma is not exhausted, they cannot seek death even if they desire it.
By what past actions were these karmic fruits received, such that sentient beings are born there?

Formerly, while among humans, they covered people with bamboo mats and led elephants to trample them; or during times of war, they constructed crushing machines to crush people; or they suspended stones on mechanical levers to drop and kill; furthermore, on dangerous paths, they set traps and pits to ensnare and kill living beings; or they used their claws and teeth to bite and gnaw upon fleas and lice—it was through such karma that they received this retribution and were born therein.
Moreover, various other unwholesome karmas lead to birth there, as do superior karmas that induce rebirth in that place.
Having been born therein, they undergo various retributions for their unwholesome karma.
Among them, the sinners have nothing left but sinews and bones, with no flesh or blood remaining. At that time, the hell-warden says to his companions:
"Now, together with you, I shall pound these sinners for the duration of a single finger-snap."
He immediately seized the various offenders and cast them into a cauldron of glowing iron, where their bodies were pounded to pieces with a red-hot iron pestle.
In the time it takes to snap one's fingers, this is equivalent to five hundred years of human life.
Undergoing such slaughter and injury, they experience the highest grade of suffering, exactly as previously described.
What karma did they perform in the past to bring about this retribution, causing sentient beings to be born there?

In former times among human beings, some wielded spears, lances, tridents, and halberds to pierce and harm sentient beings; they pounded rice, grains, sesame, and wheat together with insects for their meal. Due to such karma, they were reborn there.
Furthermore, various other unwholesome karmic retributions led to birth there, and there was also superior karma that induced birth in that place.
Having been born therein, they experience various retributions for their unwholesome karma.
Why is this hell called Saṃjīva (The Reviving)?
Because the sinners therein gather in one place, and as two mountains press together and crush them, it is named Saṃjīva.
Furthermore, this hell was originally named "Culmination" (Kūṭa), and for that reason it is called "Culmination.
He spoke again in verse:
"In the midst of the Culmination Hell, Between two great mountains,"
Countless sinners enter therein like a herd of deer;
due to the retribution of their past karma, these two mountains close together,
crushing many sentient beings, while masses of fire block them from front and back.
From the bodies of these sinners, blood flows to form rivers.
Thus they endure such suffering and hardship, unable to die in the interim.
They are placed in red iron boats and pounded with pestles.
Receiving the retribution of past karmic deeds, one remains there for five hundred years with a mere snap of the fingers.
The Tathāgata, teacher of gods and humans, seeing this as it truly is,
has therefore described the "thickets and thickets" as the dwelling place of those who commit evil.
The Chapter on the Crushing Hell is concluded. 4.
The Fourth Hell, the Howling Hell: The fourth hell is named Howling; its appearance is like a narrow chamber, numbering in the thousands.

Within that place, each sinner has a separate chamber; their bodies are large while the rooms are small, causing them intense suffering and distress as they are deprived of the four dignified postures and subjected to the torment of burning and roasting.
When this sinner descends, the fire blazes intensely; when the force of the flames is fierce, the sound of his cries is violent, and when the force of the flames is weak, the cries are faint.

Undergoing this burning and scorching, he experiences suffering of the highest degree, which is difficult to endure, extremely firm and powerful, and most excruciatingly painful; thus, until the retribution for his evil karma is fully exhausted, he cannot seek death even if he longs for it.
What past karma did they perform to receive this retribution, such that sentient beings are born there?

Formerly, while among humans, they themselves inflicted severe punishments upon those who were helpless and without refuge, or they incited others to do so; they themselves set fire to plains and wilds, or built secret chambers to kill by fire; they constructed prisons to torment people with fire; or they would burn and scorch the burrows of animals such as porcupines, pangolins, otters, foxes, and rats, even using fire to smoke out and drive away mosquitoes and gnats.

Through the retribution of such karma, they are born therein. Furthermore, there are various other evil karmic retributions for which they are born there; moreover, it is through superior karma that they are caused to be born there.
Having been born therein, they experience various retributions for their unwholesome karma.

5. The Great Screaming Hell: The fifth hell is named the Chapter on the Great Screaming Hell. "Furthermore, there is a hell named the Great Screaming Hell; its appearance is like a vast pit, immeasurable *yojanas* in breadth and length, composed entirely of red-hot iron, as previously described."

Within this place, the hell-wardens hold iron mallets in their hands, brandishing them to terrify the sinners. Upon seeing them, the sinners give rise to great fear; some flee in escape and rebellion, while others do not flee; some run about in frantic confusion, some strike their faces against the walls, some stare straight ahead, some greet them with praise, and some offer apologies and beg for mercy.
At that time, the hell-wardens asked those who had come to meet them:
"How dare you come to welcome me?
They immediately struck them with iron hammers, smashing their heads like breaking a jar of curd; the heads were shattered and the brains splattered just as the curd had been.
If anyone does not come forward to greet him, he says: "How dare you not come?
and he likewise crushes their heads as before.

Whether one wanders aimlessly or does not wander, whether one stares at the wall or looks straight ahead, and whether one rebels or does not rebel—the rules for interrogation and punishment are all like this.
For these reasons, everyone has their heads broken; none can escape it.

Experiencing these shattered fragments, the suffering of the highest grade is difficult to endure; it is extremely firm, extremely intense, and most agonizing. Thus, until the retribution for their evil karma is fully exhausted, they cannot seek death even if they long for it.
What past actions led to the reception of this retribution, causing sentient beings to be born there?

In the past, while among humans, they dug pits to serve as prisons; when offenders were placed therein, they were made unable to see the light of the sun and moon. Due to the retribution of this karma, they are born there.
Furthermore, various other evil karmic retributions lead to birth there; moreover, it is the power of superior karma that causes them to be born there.
Having been born therein, they experience the various retributions of unwholesome karma.
Furthermore, what karma did they perform to receive the retribution of having their heads crushed?

In their past lives among humans, they struck the heads of living beings, or [killed] various creatures such as fish, snakes, and centipedes; through such karmas, they receive the retribution of having their heads crushed.
The suffering of being scorched and roasted in this hell is even more severe than before, and there is the perpetual agony of having one’s head crushed.
Why is this hell named Great Wailing?

Because the sinners therein, due to being beaten and by fire, cry out with great, intense wails; they utter only sounds of great wailing without any coherent meaning, unable even to call out for their mother or father. For this reason, the hell is named Great Wailing.
Furthermore, its intrinsic nature is called "Great Screaming.
He spoke again in verse:
"In the Hell of Screaming, many people are forced into confinement; there, they are crushed together, and thus it is named 'Screaming.'"
If the fire below blazes intensely, the cries of wailing are terrifying;
if the force of the fire weakens, the sound of crying likewise subsides.
There is the suffering of having one's dignified deportment crushed and broken, as well as the agony of being scorched and roasted.
The second is the Great Screaming Hell, Deeply dark and hair-raising, with sheer walls impossible to climb; Vast and immeasurable in extent.
Within it, The hell-wardens wield red-hot iron mallets.
Their heads are crushed like those of enemies for immeasurable hundreds and thousands of years.
The Tathāgata, the Teacher of gods and humans, having seen this as it truly is,
has therefore spoken of the Two Screaming Hells, the dwelling place of those who commit evil.
The Section on the Great and Small Crying Hells is concluded.

6. The Sixth Hell: The Burning and Roasting Hell. The sixth hell is named Burning and Roasting (*Tāpana*). Its appearance is like a kiln; it is made entirely of iron, burning day and night, constantly emitting flames and light, and it extends for countless *yojanas* in breadth and length.

Within this place, there are countless tens of thousands of millions of sinners, confined and scorched; once fully cooked, they become parched both inside and out, becoming as hollow, brittle, and easily stripped away as dried meat jerky.

At that time, the gates of hell open spontaneously. Outside the gates there are countless dogs—some black, some brindled—with bodies tall and large. They wait for the gates to open, vying with one another to enter the prison; they drag out the offenders and gnaw at their bodies, devouring them at will like trees growing in reverse.

Once they have been devoured, their skin and flesh are entirely consumed, leaving only a heap of bones; in such unbearable suffering, they faint at that moment, and when a cool wind blows upon them, their skin and flesh are restored once more.

At that time, the hell-wardens again drive them back in, where they once more undergo their former sufferings of being scorched, roasted, and devoured; the supreme grades of instruments of torture are as previously described.
What past karma did these sentient beings perform to receive such retribution and be born there?

In the past, while among humans, they constructed prisons without doors or gates; they piled up earth mixed with elephant dung to form walls and floors, plastered them with mud, and used salt mixed with *gautamapā* tree oil to douse the bodies of offenders. They cast these people into the prisons where they were scorched by the sun's rays, becoming putrid, bloated, and swollen within a single night. They killed offenders by steaming or boiling them, or again by setting fires to roast them to death; they boiled silkworm cocoons or fried living beings alive. Through the retribution of such karma, they were reborn therein.
Furthermore, through various other evil karmic retributions and superior karmic retributions, they experienced birth in that place, as described above in detail.
Furthermore, by what karma is one devoured by dogs?

In a former life among humans, one raised lions, tigers, leopards, bears, brown bears, jackals, and dogs, commanding them to bite and mangle living beings. Due to such karma, one is born there; the rest is as explained above.
What past karma did he perform to obtain the touch of cool breezes?
In a former life among humans, he provided abundant meat to nourish and feed sentient beings; by virtue of this karma, he obtained the touch of cool breezes.
"Why is this hell named 'Scorching and Roasting' (Tāpana)?
Because within it, the bodies and minds of the offenders are scorched; therefore, it is named 'Scorching and Roasting.
Furthermore, its very nature is called 'Scorching and Roasting.'"
He spoke again in verse:
"In the Saṃjīva Hell, The iron houses are intensely hot;
The heat is so extreme and fierce That it is like a mass of blazing fire."
In this place, those who have committed sins are tightly packed and subjected to roasting;
according to the karma they previously performed, they undergo the retribution of suffering here.
When their bodies have thus been fully cooked, packs of dogs compete to devour them.
The skin and flesh are entirely consumed, leaving only the bones remaining.
When a cold wind blows upon them once more, the skin and flesh are restored to their original state;
the hell-wardens drive them back in again, where they must once more undergo their former sufferings.
The Tathāgata, the Teacher of gods and humans, having seen this as it truly is,
has therefore declared that this is the place where those who have committed sins dwell— the Hell of Burning and Roasting.
The Chapter on the Hell of Burning and Roasting is concluded.

7. The Great Roasting Hell. Chapter Seven: The Great Roasting Hell. Furthermore, there is a hell named Great Roasting (*Mahāpratapana*). Its appearance is like a high and vast mountain, entirely composed of red-hot iron, burning day and night and constantly emitting blazing flames.
There are sharp skewers of red-hot iron that are heated to the utmost intensity, constantly emitting flames and surrounded on all sides—above, below, and around.

Some sinners are impaled upon a single skewer and roasted against the volcanic fire; others are impaled upon two, three, ten, twenty, or even hundreds of thousands of skewers, pierced lengthwise and crosswise and roasted against the volcanic fire.
When one side has become cooked, the skewer turns of its own accord, and they roast the other side.
Furthermore, there are sinners whose iron skewers pull out of their own accord, piercing unscarred areas as they are turned over for roasting.
Furthermore, there are sinners who, due to the retribution of their most superior grade of evil karma, find that countless iron skewers all come of their own accord to pierce their bodies.

Therein, these sinners undergo this roasting on skewers; it is a most superior grade of suffering, difficult to endure, extremely firm and intense, and most agonizing. Thus, until the retribution for their evil karma is exhausted, they seek death but cannot obtain it.
What karma was performed in the past to receive this retribution?
Formerly, while among human beings, one habitually impaled and roasted living creatures over fires; due to the retribution of this karma, one was born there.
Furthermore, various other evil karmic retributions led to birth in that place, and additionally, superior karmas induced birth there.
Having been born therein, they experience various retributions for their unwholesome karma.
Why is this hell named Great Roasting (Mahātapana)?
The sinners within it are pierced by skewers and roasted from both inside and out by volcanic fires; because they are beset by grief, anxiety, and suffering, it is called Great Roasting.
Furthermore, its very nature is fundamentally that of being scorched and roasted.
He spoke again in verse:
“In the Great Scorching Hell, The sharp skewers are all made of iron;”
Surrounding the Iron Fire Mountains, brought forth by the evil karma of past lives,
those who committed wicked deeds therein are impaled in countless numbers;
like fish being grilled over and over again, they are made to suffer thus according to their karma.
The Tathāgata, teacher of gods and humans, having seen this as it truly is,
has therefore declared that the Great Burning is the dwelling place of those who commit evil.
The "Chapter on the Great Burning" is concluded.

8. The Eighth Avīci Hell: The Chapter on the Avīci Hell. Furthermore, there is a hell named Avīci. Its appearance is like that of a great city; everything is made of red iron, burning day and night and constantly emitting flames of light.
The entire eastern wall of this hell is made of red iron, burning day and night and constantly emitting flames.

The western, southern, and northern walls, as well as the upper and lower parts, are likewise ablaze. The flames from the eastern wall penetrate through to the western wall, and the flames from the western wall likewise penetrate to the eastern wall; the flames from the south reach the north, and those from the north reach the south; the flames from above reach below, and those from below reach above. Thus, the flames from all four directions fill the entirety of the hell.
Among them, there are countless thousands of sinners who undergo burning in dense layers, like stacks of firewood.

Among these, there are sinners whose bodies, due to their supreme-grade (uttama-uttama) evil karma, become massive, porous, and supple; they press against one another with heads bowed low, unable to walk or maintain the four dignified postures.
Because these sinners possess inferior or middling grades of karma from their past lives, they constantly seek liberation, running about in a state of frantic agitation.

At certain times, the eastern gate of this great hell opens of its own accord; all these sinners cry out, "The gate has opened! and vie with one another to run out in search of escape. Yet, before they have reached the gateway, the door closes by itself once more.

At that time, the western gate opened once more, and the southern and northern gates likewise opened of their own accord; these sinners cried out, "The gates have opened! and rushed toward them, but before they reached the gates, the gates closed by themselves.

Therein, these offenders undergo the great suffering of this Avīci Hell, which is difficult to endure; it is extremely firm, exceedingly intense, and most agonizing, such that as long as the retribution for their evil karma is not exhausted, they seek death but cannot obtain it.
What karma did they perform in the past to receive this retribution?
Formerly, while among humans, they may have killed their mother, killed their father, killed an arhat, shed the blood of a Buddha with a murderous intent, or caused a schism in the Saṃgha;
or perhaps their mother was already a noble one (āryā), yet they gave rise to lustful coercion toward her.

One who kills a person of the fixed group (*niyata-rāśi*), or kills a Bodhisattva being, or destroys the four kinds of *caityas* of the Tathāgata, or plunderes the property of the Saṃgha from the four quarters gathered through causes and conditions; or one who commits the most supreme grades of the ten unwholesome paths of action—killing, stealing, sexual misconduct, lying, divisive speech, harsh speech, frivolous speech, covetousness, malice, and wrong view—whether performing one, two, or all of them;
by such evil conduct, one takes birth therein. Furthermore, various karmic retributions for evil deeds arise within that birth, and moreover, superior karmas induce birth therein.
Once born therein, they experience various retributions for their unwholesome karma.
Why is this hell named Avīci?
Because within it, the offenders constantly undergo suffering without any interval or respite.
The suffering in other hells is not like this in its supreme intensity. Why is that?
In those other hells, the hell-wardens may sometimes come and sometimes not, or the great suffering may briefly cease due to cold winds.

In this hell, however, it is not so; from beginning to end one undergoes the highest grade of suffering, which is difficult to endure, being extremely firm, extremely intense, and most agonizingly acute.
In this place, the lifespan of the offenders is one kalpa, or even half a kalpa, or indefinite.

For example, it is like a furnace where iron stars and flames boil and surge throughout the entire day; the burning of the offenders' bodies is likewise so intense that it is therefore called Avīci (the Unrelenting).
Furthermore, its intrinsic nature is also called Avīci.
To restate this in verse:
"The Avīci hell is exclusively and most intensely agonizing."
Day and night it burns, its mass of flames filling every side.
Just as a single sun might burn, or an iron cauldron emitting blazing rays,
so too in Avīci, the light of fire penetrates everywhere.
Within this place, the bodies of the sinners Are like great masses of blazing fire;
You all behold the power of karma, By which they do not turn to ash or charcoal.
At times they see the gates open, And they rush out, vying with one another.
Having arrived, the gate was already closed; because the fruits of past karma were not yet exhausted.
Just as those who enjoy celestial bliss seek life and do not seek death, so too those who suffer within this realm seek death and do not seek life.
The Tathāgata, teacher of gods and humans, having seen this as it truly is,
has therefore declared that Avīci is the dwelling place for those who commit evil.
The Chapter on Avīci is concluded.
9. The Ninth Chapter on the Outer Enclosures and the Enclosing Hells. Outside the eight hells, surrounding them on all four sides, there are four successive layers of enclosing hells for each.
What are the four?
First, the Hell of Hot Ashes; second, the Hell of Excrement and Urine; third, the Hell of Sword-Leaved Trees; and fourth, the Hell of Boiling Caustic Ash.
These four layers surround [the hells] in succession; one should understand that each individual hell is likewise.
To speak of them in order, there is a hell named Hot Ashes (Uṣṇakṣāra).
When these sinners emerge from the Great Hell, they see the external hot ashes as if it were level, open ground; having seen this sign, they give rise to this thought:
"I must certainly go there now."

Thereupon, the sinner goes into that place; as his feet tread upon the hot ashes, his skin and flesh immediately rot away, just like a lump of wax cast into a fierce fire. As soon as he lifts his feet, his skin and flesh are restored once more.
At times it reaches the knees, at times the navel, at times the neck, or it sinks away until it is no longer visible.

Within this, one wanders aimlessly for countless *yojanas*, undergoing the most superior grade of suffering that is difficult to endure; it is extremely firm, intense, and most agonizing. Thus, as long as the retribution for the evil karma has not been fully exhausted, one cannot seek death even though one longs for it.

What karma was performed in the past to receive this retribution? Formerly, while among humans, they seized living beings and cast them into fire, or into hot ashes, or onto hot sand; or they committed sexual misconduct with the wives of others, transgressing worldly laws by entering the domains of others; or, having gone forth as monastics, they broke their precepts while walking, standing, sitting, or lying within the monastery grounds; or they gave rise to evil thoughts; or they trampled upon the precincts of the four types of shrines (caityas) and stepped upon the shadows of the shrines.

By the retribution of these karmas, they were born therein. Furthermore, there are various other retributions for evil karmas through which they are born there; moreover, it is the dominant karma (*adhipati-karman*) that brings about birth in those realms.
Having been born therein, they experience the various retributions of their unwholesome karma.
The second hell is named Excrement and Filth.
Within it, the sinners emerge from outside the Hell of Hot Ashes and see the excrement and filth as if it were a cool lotus pond; having seen it, they give rise to this thought:
"I must now certainly go there.

At that time, the sinner enters within; once he has entered, there are countless worms whose mouths are hard and sharp like the points of swords, boring through his skin and flesh, even reaching his tendons and bones, and devouring his marrow.
Furthermore, there are various worms that enter through the nostrils and devour the five internal organs;
or they enter through the ears, or through the eyes, or through the mouth, or through the large and small orifices, all gnawing and devouring the five internal organs.
Furthermore, there are great tigers that chew upon the sinners; once their flesh and blood are exhausted, they spit out the bones like discarded date pits.

They undergo such supreme and superior suffering, which is difficult to endure, being extremely firm, intense, and most agonizing; as long as the retribution for their evil karma is not yet exhausted, they cannot seek death even if they desire it.
What karma was performed in the past to receive this retribution?
Formerly, while among human beings, one would seize living creatures and cast them into cesspools, impure places, or even ditches; through the retribution of this karma, one is born therein.
Furthermore, one is born therein due to various other evil karmic retributions; moreover, it is through the influence of superior karmic forces that one is caused to be born there.
Having been born therein, they experience various retributions for their unwholesome karma.
What kind of karma did they perform in the past to receive this fruit of suffering, being devoured by insects?

In their former lives as humans, they either caused snakes, dogs, centipedes, crocodiles, or crocodile-like creatures to bite and chew living beings, or they gave rise to malicious intentions while indulging in the five sensory objects (*pañca-kāmaguṇa*). Due to the retribution of such karma, they are born there and undergo sufferings such as being pierced, broken, and devoured.
And he spoke in verse:
"Having crossed the hell of excrement and filth, I see a lovely grove with lush and flourishing branches; I go there, desiring to find joy."

“In this forest there are old crows, white-necked ravens, hawks, ospreys, vultures, and the like; moreover, upon this ground there are jackals, dogs, wild foxes, tigers, wolves, lions, and others, all of whom are large in body.”
These various birds and beasts gnaw and mangle the offenders, like uprooted trees devouring their own flesh; when the skin, blood, and flesh are exhausted, only the bones remain.

As the offenders undergo this pecking and injury, they experience the highest grade of suffering, which is difficult to endure, being extremely firm, intense, and most agonizing. At that moment, they faint away; then a cold wind blows, their skin and flesh grow back again, and they once more undergo being devoured. Thus they continue until their retribution is fully exhausted, at which point they cannot seek death even if they wish for it.
What karma did they perform in the past to receive this food?

In their former lives among humans, they caused tigers, wolves, and lions to devour living beings, or released hawks and dogs to hunt various birds and beasts; through such karmic actions, they were reborn there to undergo the retribution of being eaten.
There are various other evil karmic retributions for which they are reborn in that place.
What karma did they perform in the past to be blown by cold winds?

In their former lives among humans, they raised living beings, seeking to make them fat and robust for the sake of obtaining more meat; as the retribution for this karma, they are now blown by cold winds.
"The third hell is named Sword Leaves (Asipatravana).

When these sinners have crossed the Hell of Excrement and Urine (Kālasūtra) and see the Hell of Sword Leaves, their hearts give rise to a sense of attachment, as if toward a grove of mango trees (āmra-vana)."
This Path of Sword Forest is strewn with various sharp spikes, daggers, razors, and the keen edges of swords and blades covering the entire ground.
As the sinners travel along this forest path, they undergo the agonies of being pierced and impaled, until they finally enter the Great Forest.

At that time, after countless thousands of sentient beings had entered this forest, due to the causes and conditions of their evil karma, a great wind suddenly arose and rained down various weapons—namely, rains of swords, rains of arrows, rains of spears, and rains of axes—which struck wherever they landed, severing limbs and splitting heads apart, scattered in utter chaos like felled wooden staves.
Or iron spears rain down from above, piercing through the crown of the head and reaching the earth, so that one cannot move or turn.

One undergoes this supreme and highest suffering of mutilation—extremely firm, extremely intense, and most agonizing—until the retribution for the evil karma is exhausted; even seeking death, one cannot obtain it.
What karma did they perform in the past to receive this retribution?
Formerly, while among humans, they engaged in matters of combat and warfare; they provided others with swords and weapons, dispatching them to fight, saying:
"Use these implements and weapons to seize that territory; surround it on all four sides, gather many people together, and kill at will."
"By virtue of this karmic retribution, one is born there;
furthermore, there are various other types of karmic retributions through which one takes birth therein, and there is also a predominant karmic retribution that brings about birth in that place."
Having been born therein, they experience various karmic retributions for their unwholesome deeds.
This concludes the description of the Sword-Leaf Hell.
"The fourth hell is named Fierce Ash-Lye."

When these sinners emerge from the forest of sword-leaved trees, they see a cauldron of boiling ashes and think it is a cool, clear river; their hearts give rise to attachment, and they go to enter the river.

These sinners, having previously had their entire bodies torn asunder in the Forest of Swords, enter this river water; their bodies become completely rotted and destroyed until the flesh and blood are entirely gone, leaving only the tendons and bones connected together as they float and drift along with the current.

They undergo this cruel, superior-grade suffering—extremely firm, extremely intense, and most agonizing—such that as long as the retribution for their evil karma is not yet exhausted, they cannot seek death even if they desire it.
What karma was performed in the past to receive this retribution?

Formerly, while among humans, one would seize living beings and pour boiling oil over them, or sugar, or wax; or one would boil corpses and pour the resulting broth over them; or one would take an impure and defiled body into gardens or the pools and wells used by people to wash therein.

By the retribution of such karma, one is born there. Furthermore, there are various other evil karmic retributions for which one is born there; yet again, there are superior karmic retributions that induce birth in that place.
Having been born therein, they undergo the various retributions of their unwholesome karma.
On both banks of the Ashes River, there are thousands upon thousands of hell-wardens, all of immense stature, who brandish spears, tridents, and other weapons to guard over and watch the sinners.
Sometimes a sinner says to the wardens,
"Officer!
I am now greatly hungry."

The hell-wardens then seize them with forks and hurl them onto the bank; or they use tongs and hooks to pry open their mouths and thrust glowing iron balls, constantly emitting flames, into their mouths. Their lips and mouths are scorched and burned, and as the balls pass through the throat, chest, heart, abdomen, the five viscera, and the intestines and stomach, all these organs are completely rotted away until the balls emerge from below.

These sinners undergo such cruel torment; the suffering of the highest grade is difficult to endure, being extremely firm, intense, and most agonizing. Thus they continue until their retribution for evil karma is exhausted, at which point they cannot even seek death.
What karma was performed in the past to receive this retribution?

Formerly, while among humans, one may have given poisoned food to others or administered aconite to kill them; or, having left the household life, one may have broken the precepts and consumed the offerings of the state; or one may have engaged in false speech and harsh words—it is through such karmas that one receives this retribution and is born therein.

Furthermore, there are various other evil karmic retributions for which one is born there; moreover, it is through these predominant karmas (*adhipati-karman*) that one is induced to be born in that place.
Having been born therein, they experience various retributions for their unwholesome karma.
At times, the offenders say to the wardens:
"Officer!..."
"I am now greatly parched with thirst.

The hell-warden then seizes the offender with a fork and hurls him onto the bank; or, using tongs and hooks, he forces open his mouth and pours molten iron liquid, which is constantly ablaze with flames, into it. His lips and mouth are scorched and burned, and as the liquid passes through his throat, chest, heart, abdomen, the five viscera, and intestines, they all rot and dissolve until the liquid flows out from below.

At that time, the sinner undergoes this cruel torment; the suffering of the highest grade is difficult to endure, being extremely firm, intense, and most agonizing, such that as long as the retribution of their evil karma is not exhausted, they cannot seek death even if they desire it.

What karma did they perform in the past to undergo this suffering of sin? Formerly, while among humans, they took the urine of elephants, horses, and other animals and poured it into the mouths and noses of others;

or they doused their noses and mouths with the pungent juices of the five spices; or they placed poison in drinks and forced others to consume it; or they encouraged others to drink various kinds of alcohol; or for profit they sold liquor or drank it themselves; or having left the household life, they broke the precepts and consumed the offerings of the land, such as ghee, oil, sugar, and honey; or they drank what others were unfit to drink. Through the retribution of these karmas, they were born there;
furthermore, through various other evil karmic retributions, they were born there; and through superior karmic retributions, they were caused to be born in that place.
Having been born therein, they experience various other retributions for their unwholesome karma.
He spoke again in verse:
"The sinner, having emerged from the great prison, Sees this place of hot ashes."
Just as upon a level and broad ground, one who gives rise to craving goes straight toward it;
having arrived, they run about wildly for countless yojanas,
their feet rotting from being raised and lowered, as they undergo the most intense suffering.
Having emerged from the Hell of Hot Ashes, one immediately beholds a pit of excrement, a hundred fathoms wide, long, and deep;
out of craving, one mistakes it for a pond of flowers.
Within it dwell countless worms, their mouths as hard and sharp as blades.
Wearing skins and eating flesh and blood, breaking tendons and bones to consume the marrow;
having emerged from the pit of excrement, they see the Forest of Swords and conceive a craving for it,
thinking its branches and twigs are tender and lush, and go there desiring to find pleasure.
In the forest are various kinds of birds, their beaks as sharp as needles;
they seize people like living trees and devour their flesh and blood.
Once they have finished eating, only the bones and sinews remain.
When a cold wind blows, the skin and flesh are restored once more.
In terror they leap and bound about; in places of suffering, they conceive thoughts of peace.
Along the way they suffer injury and harm, entering the fearsome Forest of Swords.
At that time, the body is rent asunder; with extreme agony, a torrent of blood flows forth.
Having emerged from this forest, one immediately enters the River of Ashes;
like beans boiling and bubbling, one sinks or floats, tossing about.
Within the boiling, seething lye, the sinners are likewise.
The various hell-wardens on both banks seize their bodies with forks and pierce them;
they are dragged out and placed upon the ground, where they are forced to swallow iron pellets.
Or again, molten iron liquid is sought and poured into their mouths;
it burns and sears the interior of their entire bodies before exiting from below.
Those who have committed such evil deeds undergo this suffering in this hell.
In the past, you did not cultivate wholesome karma, but practiced the crooked path of error.
By giving rise to right reflection, you are able to abandon all evil deeds;
practicing exclusively in wholesome conduct, such a person crosses over the evil realms.
Knowing that the fruits and retributions of the two types of karma—good and evil—are distinct, the wise person should abandon evil and plant all manner of roots of goodness.
Furthermore, there is another practice: the eightfold path of the noble ones.
To extinguish all suffering, one contemplates these four dharmas without remainder.
Having seen this as it truly is, the Tathāgata, teacher of gods and humans,
spoke of the garden-enclosed prison as the dwelling place of those who commit evil.
The section on the Garden Enclosing Hell is concluded. 10.
The Tenth Chapter: The Hell of Yama. This chapter on the Hell of Yama is as spoken by the Buddha, the Bhagavat, and the Arhats.
Thus have I heard.
At one time the Buddha, the World-Honored One, said: "Bhikṣus!

With the divine eye, purified and surpassing that of humans, I see sentient beings passing away and being reborn—those of beautiful or ugly appearance, those sublime or base, and those dwelling in good or evil realms; I know them as they truly are, according to the karma by which they take birth.
And he spoke in verse:
“Having given rise to an evil mind, And having uttered crooked speech,
Or having performed an evil physical act— All because of past heedlessness.”
"Having heard little and possessing no merit, one commits evil during the brevity of life;
such a person, upon casting off body and life, shall immediately fall into the Yama hell.
Thus the Buddha told the bhikṣus:

"If a person in their past lives failed to show reverence to their parents, śramaṇas, and brāhmaṇas; failed to show reverence to friends, elders, and superiors; failed to cultivate right goodness and meritorious deeds; felt no dread toward present evils and future transgressions; failed to practice giving or cultivate merit; did not observe the eightfold fast or uphold the five precepts—then after they have relinquished their life-span and been born in hell, the wardens will seize them and deliver them to Yama, saying:”

"In the past, this person did not show reverence to their parents, śramaṇas, or brāhmaṇas; they did not honor their friends, kin, or elders; they did not cultivate wholesome deeds or meritorious practices; they felt no dread toward evil in the present life nor toward sin in future lives; they did not practice giving or cultivate merit; they did not observe the eightfold fast nor uphold the five precepts."
"I pray that Your Majesty will instruct this person so that they may recognize the causes and effects of good and evil.
Then King Yama, following the teaching of the five heavenly messengers, gave righteous instruction and said to the sentient being:
"Did you not previously see the first heavenly messenger go among those in the human realm?"
“Great King! I did not see it before.
The king said:
"In the past, when you were among humans, did you not see young children and infants, newly born and lying on their backs, unable to avoid the damp or seek out the dry?
The sentient beings replied,
"Dharma King!"
"I have already seen it before.
The king said, "Regarding your insight and understanding, why do you not reflect and consider this: [text missing]"

I am now born; for me, who has not yet transcended the nature of birth, I should, according to my ability, practice wholesome dharmas through body, speech, and mind, so that over a long period of time I may attain the benefit and joy of the True Path.
The sentient beings said:
"Great King!
In the past we were negligent and were unable to practice virtue."
The King said:

"Your evil karma was created and nurtured by yourself; it was not created by your parents, nor by the king, nor by the gods, nor by your deceased ancestors, nor by śramaṇas or brāhmaṇas. You created it and you must experience its consequences; though you did not wish for them, their retribution will certainly arrive."

Then King Yama, having finished his reprimand and instruction by means of this first divine messenger, further, by means of the second divine messenger who gave a correct and virtuous admonition, said to the sentient beings:
"Did you not previously see the second divine messenger go among those humans?"
“Great King! I did not see it before.
The king said:

"In your former existence among humans, did you not see men or women who were aged, great, or advanced in years; or perhaps those with sores on their backs like drawn horn-bows, walking forward supported by staffs, their entire bodies trembling?"
The sentient beings said,
"Great King!
We have indeed seen it before."
The King said:
"Since you possess such understanding, why do you not reflect:

'I am now subject to old age, yet I have not transcended the law of aging; I ought to practice wholesome dharmas according to my ability through body, speech, and mind, so that for a long time I may attain the benefit and joy of the True Path.'"
The sentient beings said,
"Great King!
In the past we were heedless and were unable to practice virtue."
The King said:

"Your evil karma was created and increased by yourself; it was not created by your parents, nor by the king, nor by the gods, nor by deceased ancestors, nor by śramaṇas and brāhmaṇas. You created it and you must experience its results; though you did not wish for them, their retribution will certainly arrive."

Then King Yama, having finished reprimanding and instructing him through this first divine messenger, further instructed and exhorted him correctly through the third divine messenger, saying to the sentient being:
"Did you not previously see the third divine messenger go among those people?"
“Great King! I did not see it before.
The king said:

"In the past, when you were among humans, did you not see men and women suffering from illness and affliction in extreme distress—some confined to their beds, some propped up on stools, and some sleeping on the ground; this bodily experience of suffering being most firm, most intense, difficult to endure, and difficult to bear, as it encroaches upon one's lifespan and is beset by manifold sufferings?"
"Great King! I have indeed seen it before.
The king said:
"Since you have already understood this, why do you not reflect:

'I am currently afflicted by illness; I have not yet transcended the nature of illness. I should, according to my ability, practice wholesome dharmas through body, speech, and mind, so that for a long time I may attain the benefit and joy of the True Path.'"
The sentient beings said:
"Great King!
In the past, we were negligent and were unable to practice virtue."
The King said:

"You have committed these evil deeds yourself and must suffer their consequences yourself; they were not created by your parents, nor by the king, nor by the gods, nor by your deceased ancestors, nor by śramaṇas or brahmins. You created them yourself and must suffer them yourself; though you did not wish for it, the retribution of karma will inevitably arrive."

Then King Yama, having finished rebuking and instructing them through this first divine messenger, further instructed and exhorted them correctly by means of the fourth divine messenger, saying to the sentient beings:
"Did you not previously see the fourth divine messenger go among those people?"
“Great King! I did not see him before.
The king said:

"In the past, when you were among humans, did you not see men or women who died on the first day, or the second, third, or even up to the seventh day, becoming bloated, or turning dark blue-black, or putrefying with a foul odor, or being devoured by birds and beasts?"
The sentient beings said:
"Great King!
We have indeed seen it before."
The King said:
"Since you possess understanding, why do you not reflect:

'I am now subject to death and have not yet transcended the law of mortality; I ought to practice wholesome dharmas according to my ability through body, speech, and mind, so that for a long time I may attain the benefit and joy of the True Path.'"
The sentient beings said:
"Great King!
In the past, we were heedless and were unable to practice virtue."
The King said:

"Your evil karma was created and nurtured by yourself; it was not created by your parents, nor by the king, nor by the gods, nor by deceased ancestors, nor by śramaṇas or brāhmaṇas. You created it and you must experience its results; though you did not wish for them, their retribution will certainly arrive."
Then King Yama, having finished reprimanding and instructing them through this fifth divine messenger, further gave them a correct and virtuous admonition by addressing the sentient beings, saying:
"Did you not previously see the fifth divine messenger go among those people?"
“Great King! I did not see it before.
The king said:

"In the past, when you were among humans, did you not see people who, having committed the sins of killing, stealing, sexual misconduct, or even lying and harsh speech, were arrested by the king's men? With their hair matted and heads bound, they were paraded through the four crossroads with drums beating as a public proclamation, led out through the southern city gate to the place of execution. Seated beneath the execution post, they were punished in various ways according to the gravity of their crimes—whether by staff or whip, by the amputation of hands or feet, by the cutting off of ears or nose, or even by capital punishment."
The sentient beings said:
"Great King!
We have seen it before."
The King said:
"You possess discernment and understanding; why do you not reflect upon this?

All evil karma yields visible retribution in the present life. I am now subject to karma and act according to the force of my deeds; whatever karma I have performed, whether good or evil, will lead to rebirth in a future world accordingly."
The sentient beings said:
"Great King!
In the past we were heedless and were unable to practice virtue."
The King said:

"Your evil karma was created and increased by yourself; it was not created by your parents, nor by the king, nor by the gods, nor by the deceased ancestors, nor by śramaṇas or brāhmaṇas. You created it and you must receive its fruit; though you did not wish for it, its retribution will certainly arrive."
Having spoken these words, he set aside his mind and remained still.
At that time, the hell-wardens seized this sinner and, suspending him head-downward, cast him into the Saṃjīva Hell.
This hell has four corners and four gates; it is surrounded by an iron city, both above and below which are made of iron, burning day and night and constantly emitting flames of light.

Therein, the sinners follow the realm of the Black Rope (Kālasūtra) and undergo being hacked by saws and axes; their flesh and blood are entirely exhausted until only sinews and bones remain. Their suffering is unbearable, and they faint and die for a moment; then, a cold wind blows, and their flesh and blood are restored once more.
Experiencing these most intense and supreme sufferings of harm, they cannot seek death even when the retribution for their evil karma has not yet been fully exhausted.
What karma did they perform in the past to receive such a retribution, causing sentient beings to be born there?

In former times, while among human beings, they were arrogant toward their parents, śramaṇas, and brahmins; they failed to show respect to friends, relatives, and elders; they did not cultivate wholesome virtues or meritorious deeds; they felt no fear regarding present evils or future transgressions; they did not practice giving or cultivate merit; they did not observe the eightfold fast nor uphold the five precepts. Due to such inferior karma, they were born there to undergo these various harms and sufferings.

Next, those of an even more intensified grade are born in the second hell, Black Rope; next, those of an even more intensified grade are born in the third hell, Crushing; next, those of yet another intensified grade are born in the fourth hell, Screaming; next, those of yet another intensified grade are born in the fifth hell, Great Screaming; next, those of an intensified grade are born in the sixth hell, Heating; next, those of yet another intensified grade are born in the seventh hell, Great Heating; and finally, those of the most intensified grade are born in the eighth hell, Avīci.
This Vīci Hell has four corners and four gates, surrounded by an iron city with walls of iron above and below, burning day and night and filled everywhere with flames.

Within it, hundreds of thousands of countless sinners undergo torment in dense layers; like a stack of firewood or like smelting iron, their bodies are scorched in this manner for the duration of a full day and night.
The Buddha said: "Bhikṣus!

In this Vīci Hell, sometimes the eastern gate opens briefly. When the offenders see it, they run toward the gate, seeking a place of refuge, seeking a place of rescue, and seeking deliverance; yet before they have reached the gate, the gate has already closed again."
The same occurs at the western, southern, and northern gates.

Having witnessed these things, their hopes and expectations are severed; their bodies and minds are afflicted with suffering, and they wail in grief and agony. For immeasurable thousands of years, they constantly endure such supreme and intense suffering, which is difficult to bear and most excruciating. Thus, until the retribution of their evil karma has been fully exhausted, they cannot seek death even though they long for it.
What past actions led to the reception of this retribution?
Formerly, while among humans, they slandered and mocked diligent sages; or they betrayed acts of kindness and righteousness, or committed treachery and murder against beloved friends.
This Great Avīci Hell is the primary locus for the maturation of karma; beings are born therein due to the causes of skillful means [of past actions].
Furthermore, they are born therein as a result of various evil karmic retributions; moreover, it is through the influence of superior karmas that one is caused to be born within it.
Having been born there, they experience various kinds of unwholesome retributions.
Once they have exhausted their primary retribution and emerged from the great hell, due to the remnants of their karma, they enter the Four Enclosures.

First, they enter hot ashes that reach deep down to their knees; once the knees have sunk in, they are scorched and rotted away like wax thrown into a fire, yet when they lift their feet, the skin and flesh are restored as before.

Within this place, the sinners seek refuge, rescue, and escape, wandering aimlessly for countless *yojanas*. They see a pit of excrement, its ground entirely filled with filth and dead corpses. Inside it dwell worms called *Karkoṭaka*, numbering immeasurably; they resemble long snakes, with white bodies, black heads, and mouths like the edge of a sword. Raising their heads and gaping wide, they wait for the arrival of the sinners.
Once the sinner has entered, these insects pierce the skin, penetrate the flesh, and reach the bone to devour the marrow.
While undergoing this suffering, they cry out in constant wailing for countless thousands of years; even when their evil karma is not yet exhausted, they seek death but cannot obtain it.

Having emerged from this hell, he sees the Forest of Sword-leaves; seeking refuge, rescue, and escape, he runs swiftly toward the forest, his body and feet being pierced and torn by various sharp thorns along the way.

Next, they enter the Forest of Swords. At that time, a hot wind blows, shaking the sword-trees; when the wind touches them, it is like fire, scorching and rotting their entire bodies. Furthermore, the Forest of Swords rains down various weapons that hack and pierce their bodies, so that wherever they strike, neither skin nor flesh remains.
They endure this torment for countless thousands of years, constantly crying out in agony; until their evil karma is exhausted, they seek death but cannot find it.
Furthermore, various birds and beasts devour their bodies, as previously described.

Having emerged from this hell, they see a river of hot caustic ash overflowing and surging with boiling heat; seeking refuge, rescue, and escape, they run headlong into the river, wallowing and tossing about like beans being boiled.
At the edge, there are hell-wardens holding iron nets; they sift out the sinners and deposit them on a shore of glowing red iron.
The wardens ask: "Sinner!"
"What do you require?
The sinner replied,
"I am now so hungry that I cannot endure it."
At that time, the hell-wardens immediately pry open his mouth with iron tongs and cast in a glowing iron ball.
Wherever the ball reaches, the lips, tongue, heart, chest, intestines, and stomach—all five viscera—are completely scorched and consumed; the ball then passes straight through and exits below.
When he thirsts and drinks molten iron, it is likewise.
